hunks.baseline: *This is driving me crazy.*
hunks.sol: *This is driving me insane.*

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin felt the world go yellow before his eyes.
hunks.sol: The world went yellow before Hyuk Mujin’s eyes.

hunks.baseline: Assassins disguised as disciples from minor sects. The Head Elder’s betrayal. That alone was enough to make his head feel like it was about to explode, but…
hunks.sol: Assassins disguised as disciples of minor sects. The Head Elder’s betrayal. That alone was enough to make his head explode, but…

hunks.baseline: *Why the hell did this guy collapse too?!*
hunks.sol: *Why the hell did this man collapse too?!*

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung had gone down out of nowhere. The reconnaissance squad had taken turns slapping his cheeks and shaking him by the collar, and he still showed no sign of waking.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung had suddenly lost consciousness. The reconnaissance squad members had taken turns slapping his cheeks and shaking him by the collar, but he showed no sign of waking up.

hunks.baseline: It was enough to make a ghost weep. And with things as they were, Hyuk Mujin—the deputy squad leader—had ended up in charge of this enormous mess.
hunks.sol: It made no damn sense. And with things as they were, Hyuk Mujin—the deputy squad leader—had somehow ended up in charge of this colossal mess.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk picked out two of the reconnaissance squad members still standing there in a daze.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin pointed to two of the reconnaissance squad members still standing there in a daze.

hunks.baseline: “Return to the main family at once and report this.”
hunks.sol: “You two, return to the family at once and report what happened.”

hunks.baseline: He did not know why the family’s senior, a hero of the old Great Faction War, had devised such a dark scheme, or what he hoped to gain from it.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin didn’t know why one of the family’s most respected elders, a hero of the Great Faction War, had devised such a scheme or what he hoped to gain from it.

hunks.baseline: But they had to stop the worst from coming to pass.
hunks.sol: But they had to prevent the worst from happening.

hunks.baseline: “The rest of us move to the main force. Hurry!”
hunks.sol: “Everyone else, move out for the main force. Hurry!”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk hoisted the unconscious Jin Taekyung onto his back.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin hoisted the unconscious Jin Taekyung onto his back.

hunks.baseline: After running for roughly two hours, the world went yellow before his eyes again—this time for a different reason.
hunks.sol: After roughly two hours of running, the world went yellow before his eyes again—this time for a different reason.

hunks.baseline: It had only been a few days since Jopil’s brutal palm strike had left him with internal injuries. He had loudly told Jin Taekyung he was almost fully recovered, but in truth he needed at least two weeks of rest, no arguments.
hunks.sol: It had only been a few days since Jopil’s brutal palm strike had left him with internal injuries. He had boasted to Jin Taekyung that he was almost fully recovered, but in truth, he needed at least two weeks of complete rest.

hunks.baseline: “Huff… huff.”
hunks.sol: “Huff, huff.”

hunks.baseline: He was soaked through, and his legs were shaking.
hunks.sol: His entire body was drenched, and his legs were trembling.

hunks.baseline: He would have fallen behind even if he had only been trying to keep up. Carrying the solidly built Jin Taekyung on his back was literally killing him.
hunks.sol: He would have struggled to keep up even without a burden. With the solidly built Jin Taekyung on his back, he felt ready to drop dead.

hunks.baseline: Now he was even hallucinating his parents—who were alive and well—waving him over. The woman standing beside them was a face he often saw at the temple hall.
hunks.sol: Now he was even hallucinating his parents—both alive and well—beckoning to him. The middle-aged woman standing beside them looked familiar from the temple prayer hall.

hunks.baseline: “Child. You’ve suffered enough. You may rest now.”
hunks.sol: “Child. You have suffered enough. You may rest now.”

hunks.baseline: Her benevolent smile slowly eased Hyuk’s heart.
hunks.sol: Her benevolent smile slowly put Hyuk Mujin’s heart at ease.

hunks.baseline: *Yeah. I’ve done enough. The squad leader collapses at the critical moment, and these bastards won’t even offer to carry him for me, whether I drop dead or not.*
hunks.sol: *Yeah. I’ve done enough. The squad leader keels over at the most important moment, and these bastards don’t even offer to carry him, whether I drop dead or not.*

hunks.baseline: Hyuk was just about to let go when—
hunks.sol: Just as Hyuk Mujin was about to let go—

hunks.baseline: Warm breath slipped into his ear. He knew who it was without turning around. Tears of relief stung Hyuk’s eyes.
hunks.sol: Warm breath tickled his ear. He knew who it was without turning around. Tears of relief sprang to Hyuk Mujin’s eyes.

hunks.baseline: Blood and screams burst out on every side. A blood-soaked martial artist crawled on all fours between the corpses.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed and screams erupted on every side. A blood-soaked martial artist crawled on all fours between the corpses.

hunks.baseline: His still-youthful face was stained with pain and terror.
hunks.sol: His still-youthful face was twisted with pain and terror.

hunks.baseline: He tried to hold it back, but the crying kept breaking free. He had spent ten years grinding through martial arts with grim determination, and it had all been useless on a battlefield spraying blood.
hunks.sol: He tried to hold back his sobs, but they kept bursting out. He had spent ten years gritting his teeth and honing his martial arts, yet it had all proved useless on this blood-soaked battlefield.

hunks.baseline: The senior he had counted on was dead. So was the comrade who had been like a brother. Weapons poured in from every direction, splitting open bellies and hacking limbs apart.
hunks.sol: The senior he had relied on was dead. So was the comrade who had been like a brother to him. Weapons had poured in from every direction, splitting open bellies and hacking limbs apart.

hunks.baseline: He called for her without end, and then his face went stiff.
hunks.sol: He called for his mother over and over until his face suddenly went rigid.

hunks.baseline: A spearhead had already sprouted from his chest.
hunks.sol: A spearhead had sprouted from his chest.

hunks.baseline: His eyes flew wide for an instant, then the light went out of them. A wandering martial artist with a bandit’s beard pulled his rusty spear free and grinned.
hunks.sol: His eyes flew wide for an instant, then the light faded from them. A wandering martial artist with a bandit’s beard pulled out the rusty spear and grinned.

hunks.baseline: But even a wandering martial artist who had survived countless brushes with death could not dodge the blade that came flying at him a moment later.
hunks.sol: But even a wandering martial artist who had survived countless brushes with death could not evade the blade that came flying at him the next instant.

hunks.baseline: A silver line flashed, and the wandering martial artist’s head shot into the air.
hunks.sol: A silver line flashed, and the wandering martial artist’s head flew into the air.

hunks.baseline: Nameless men killed and died on every side, over and over.
hunks.sol: Nameless men killed and were killed on every side, over and over again.

hunks.baseline: That was what a battlefield was.
hunks.sol: That was a battlefield.

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder looked out over the battlefield, his face steeped in memory.
hunks.sol: The Head Elder gazed across the battlefield, lost in memory.

hunks.baseline: Eight Spring Gorge. A battleground that had occupied a single line in the history of the Great Faction War, decades ago. How many had died in that narrow gorge?
hunks.sol: Eight Spring Gorge. A fierce battleground that had earned a single line in the history of the Great Faction War decades ago. How many people had died in that narrow gorge?

hunks.baseline: His body had been strong, and his heart had burned hot. It had been a time when that embarrassing character—chivalry—had still felt enormous.
hunks.sol: His body had been strong, and his heart had burned hot. It was a time when that embarrassing word—*chivalry*—had still seemed grand.

hunks.baseline: But the Great Faction War had changed the Head Elder. He had grown tired of the endless fighting, and afraid of death.
hunks.sol: But the Great Faction War had changed the Head Elder. He had grown weary of the endless fighting and afraid of death.

hunks.baseline: *What good is a chivalrous warrior? Die, and you’re nothing but a ghost.*
hunks.sol: *What good is a chivalrous warrior? Once you die, you’re nothing but a ghost.*

hunks.baseline: That had been a sliver of enlightenment. In the end he had survived and become a hero, and after a long stretch of endurance he had reached this place.
hunks.sol: That realization had been a kind of enlightenment. In the end, he had survived and become a hero. After long years of bitter endurance, he had finally reached this point.

hunks.baseline: Now it was time to reap the fruit.
hunks.sol: Now it was time to reap the fruits of his labor.

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder turned his cunning old eyes on the man standing beside him.
hunks.sol: The Head Elder turned his shrewd old eyes toward the man standing beside him.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung was a remarkable talent. He was young, his martial arts were considerable, and above all he had the dignity and judgment a leader needed. He sometimes let himself be bound by sentiment, but perhaps because of that, he was deeply respected within the family.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung was an exceptional talent. He was young, highly accomplished in martial arts, and above all, possessed the dignity and judgment required of a leader. At times he allowed sentiment to sway him, but perhaps because of that, he was deeply respected within the family.

hunks.baseline: *He’s more than capable of raising the family.*
hunks.sol: *He is more than capable of restoring the family to greatness.*

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder caught himself and let out a short laugh.
hunks.sol: The Head Elder caught himself and let out a quiet laugh.

hunks.baseline: What a bizarre thing to be thinking, this far along. Jin Taekyung would already have died and become a lonely ghost, at that.
hunks.sol: What a strange thing to be thinking after coming this far. Besides, Jin Taekyung was surely dead by now, reduced to a lonely ghost.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung reacted to the quiet mutter.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung reacted to the quiet murmur.

hunks.baseline: “Nothing of importance. Old men talk to themselves more. More to the point, how does it look to you, Lesser Family Head?”
hunks.sol: “Nothing of importance. Old men tend to talk to themselves. More importantly, how does the situation look to you, Lesser Family Head?”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened slightly. They held the advantage in troop quality and terrain, but the casualties kept mounting.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung’s expression darkened slightly. They held the advantage in both troop quality and terrain, but their casualties continued to mount.

hunks.baseline: There was no way he could watch members of his family die and feel at ease.
hunks.sol: There was no way he could watch members of his family die and remain unmoved.

hunks.baseline: “Lesser Family Head. I understand how you feel, but do not act rashly.”
hunks.sol: “Lesser Family Head. I understand how you feel, but you must not act rashly.”

hunks.baseline: “A leader must know when to step forward. The longer the battle drags on, the more impatient they become. That is the moment we have to seize.”
hunks.sol: “A leader must know when to step forward. The longer the battle drags on, the more impatient our enemies will become. That is the moment we must seize.”

hunks.baseline: “The Mount Heng Sword Sect will soon throw its full strength at us.”
hunks.sol: “The Mount Heng Sword Sect will soon commit its full strength.”

hunks.baseline: “They’ll put their Peak masters at the front. Their Sect Leader, Lee Cheonbaek, may even come himself.”
hunks.sol: “They’ll place their Peak masters at the front. Their Sect Leader, Lee Cheonbaek, may even come himself.”

hunks.baseline: “If you, I, and Wipeng hold off the enemy command, and arrows rain down from the cliffs, their morale will hit rock bottom.”
hunks.sol: “If you, Wipeng, and I hold off their leaders while arrows rain down from the cliffs, their morale will plummet.”

hunks.baseline: “It’s a shame we can’t use a fire attack. I resent the heavens.”
hunks.sol: “It’s a shame we can’t use fire. I resent the heavens.”

hunks.baseline: The narrow terrain of Eight Spring Gorge was perfect for fire, but the heavy snowfall from several days ago had left snowdrifts everywhere.
hunks.sol: The narrow terrain of Eight Spring Gorge was perfect for a fire attack, but the heavy snowfall several days earlier had left snow piled everywhere.

hunks.baseline: Even if the heavens had taken Jin Wikyung’s side, though, what he was hoping for would never have happened.
hunks.sol: Yet even if the heavens had sided with Jin Wikyung, what he hoped for would never have happened.

hunks.baseline: The men drawing their bows on the cliffs would obey the Head Elder.
hunks.sol: The men drawing their bows atop the cliffs would obey the Head Elder’s commands.

hunks.baseline: The years of waiting had been too long. He resented the destiny that had only now arrived.
hunks.sol: He had waited far too many years. He resented Heaven’s mandate for arriving only now.

hunks.baseline: The sight of Hyuk Mujin’s ugly face sent a rush of relief through me. The other reconnaissance squad members crowding in at the news that I was awake were no different.
hunks.sol: A rush of relief swept through me at the sight of Hyuk Mujin’s ugly face. I felt the same about the other reconnaissance squad members who crowded around when they heard I was awake.

hunks.baseline: I’d have to deal with the bastard who had just said that later. I memorized his face and name, then grinned at everyone.
hunks.sol: I’d deal with the bastard who’d just said that later. I memorized his face and name, then grinned at everyone.

hunks.baseline: “Did he hit his head?”
hunks.sol: “Did he hurt his head?”

hunks.baseline: “His head—check his head!”
hunks.sol: “His head! Check his head!”

hunks.baseline: But it was also a greeting I’d genuinely wanted to give them at least once.
hunks.sol: Still, it was a greeting I’d genuinely wanted to give them at least once.

hunks.baseline: …Not that they didn’t treat me like a lunatic afterward.
hunks.sol: …Even if they did treat me like a lunatic for it.

hunks.baseline: “Anyway, that’s enough greeting. How long was I out?”
hunks.sol: “Anyway, that’s enough greetings. How long was I out?”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk dropped onto the ground with a thud and answered.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin dropped to the ground with a thud and answered.

hunks.baseline: “Definitely more than an hour, and a little under two.”
hunks.sol: “Definitely more than an hour, but a little under two.”

hunks.baseline: I’d spent two weeks in reality, so the timing roughly lined up. I nodded and moved on.
hunks.sol: I’d spent two weeks in reality, so the timing roughly lined up. I nodded and moved on to my next question.

hunks.baseline: “Why are you asking that all of a sudden? Seriously.”
hunks.sol: “Why are you suddenly asking that? Seriously.”

hunks.baseline: “No time. Answer.”
hunks.sol: “We don’t have time. Just answer me.”

hunks.baseline: “You were breathing, that’s why you woke up. Otherwise you’d be dead.”
hunks.sol: “You were breathing, so you woke up. Otherwise, you’d be dead.”

hunks.baseline: Apparently, logging in or logging out put the other side into a deathlike sleep.
hunks.sol: Apparently, logging in or logging out left the body on the other side in a deathlike state.

hunks.baseline: *If I’d logged out before dealing with the assassins, there wouldn’t have been a body to come back to.*
hunks.sol: *If I’d logged out before dealing with the assassins, there wouldn’t have been a body left to come back to.*

hunks.baseline: I’d think about that later.
hunks.sol: I could think about that later.

hunks.baseline: “We were already heading that way. We split two men off and sent them back to the family.”
hunks.sol: “We were already heading there. I split off two men and sent them back to the family.”

hunks.baseline: “Uh, Squad Leader. I’m sorry to say this, but… I think we have to consider the worst case.”
hunks.sol: “Uh, Squad Leader. I’m sorry to say this, but… I think we have to consider the worst-case scenario.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin and every member of the reconnaissance squad clamped their mouths shut. Nobody had to ask what the worst case meant.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin and every member of the reconnaissance squad fell silent. No one needed to ask what the worst-case scenario meant.

hunks.baseline: From what Gwak Jun had said right before he died, this betrayal had been planned down to the last detail for a long time.
hunks.sol: According to what Gwak Jun had said just before he died, this betrayal had been meticulously planned for a long time.

hunks.baseline: But the plan had exactly one error.
hunks.sol: But the plan contained exactly one mistake.

hunks.baseline: No—maybe, in another way, he’d overestimated me. He’d sent dozens of First Rate masters just to kill me.
hunks.sol: No—maybe, in a way, he had overestimated me. He’d sent dozens of First Rate masters just to kill me.

hunks.baseline: On top of that, when Gwak Jun first showed his true colors, he’d said they had to start moving soon if they wanted to make it on time.
hunks.sol: On top of that, when Gwak Jun first revealed his true colors, he’d said they needed to start moving soon if they wanted to make it on time.

hunks.baseline: I met each squad member’s eyes and spoke firmly.
hunks.sol: I met each squad member’s gaze and spoke firmly.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t think about the worst case. I’ll change that outcome, no matter what it takes.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t think about the worst-case scenario. No matter what it takes, I’ll change the outcome.”

hunks.baseline: I gave Hyuk’s choked-up face a good-natured smile.
hunks.sol: I gave the emotional Hyuk Mujin a warm smile.

hunks.baseline: “Want to get beaten to death instead?”
hunks.sol: “Want me to beat you to death instead?”

hunks.baseline: “Run even one more step in the time we’ve got. Don’t you know marathon spirit?”
hunks.sol: “Run one more step while we still have time. Haven’t you ever heard of marathon spirit?”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t.”
hunks.sol: “I haven’t.”

hunks.baseline: “Anyway, get up. Another hour will do it.”
hunks.sol: “Anyway, get up. We’ll be there in another hour.”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk grabbed his shaking legs and pushed himself up, then cocked his head.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin gripped his trembling legs and forced himself upright, then cocked his head.

hunks.baseline: “I already told you. Even at full speed, it’s two hours.”
hunks.sol: “I already told you. Even at full speed, it’ll take two.”

hunks.baseline: “Exactly. An hour.”
hunks.sol: “Exactly. One hour.”

hunks.baseline: “What are you even saying…”
hunks.sol: “What are you even talking about…?”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk blinked at me, as simple as an ox. I smiled even brighter.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin blinked at me, guileless as an ox. I smiled even brighter.

hunks.baseline: “You ever heard of grit?”
hunks.sol: “Ever heard of grit?”

hunks.baseline: Two hours or four, I didn’t care.
hunks.sol: Whether it should take two hours or four didn’t matter.

hunks.baseline: We were getting there in an hour. Period.
hunks.sol: We were getting there in one. Period.

hunks.baseline: “Casualties are heavy. Sect Leader, please take action.”
hunks.sol: “Our casualties are mounting. Sect Leader, please take action.”

hunks.baseline: Even as the reports kept coming, Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek, Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, did not open his eyes.
hunks.sol: Despite the continuing reports, Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek, Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect, kept his eyes closed.

hunks.baseline: The war had started in a rush, and the preparations had been just as thin. Provisions were burning down fast, morale was dropping, and deserters were popping up one after another.
hunks.sol: The war had begun in a rush, and their preparations had been equally inadequate. Their provisions were rapidly dwindling, morale was falling, and men were deserting one after another.

hunks.baseline: *They read us completely.*
hunks.sol: *They saw right through me.*

hunks.baseline: Rage at losing his son and impatience with the situation had clouded his judgment. He had ignored his subordinates’ advice and taken the fastest route he could find.
hunks.sol: Rage over the loss of his son and impatience with the situation had clouded his judgment. He had ignored his subordinates’ advice and chosen the fastest route.

hunks.baseline: And that was how he had run into the Jin Family of Taiyuan in a narrow gorge whose very name was unfamiliar: Eight Spring Gorge.
hunks.sol: That was how he had ended up confronting the Jin Family of Taiyuan in a narrow gorge whose very name was unfamiliar to him: Eight Spring Gorge.

hunks.baseline: The fearsome vision of a Peak master pierced the battlefield.
hunks.sol: The formidable vision of a Peak master swept across the battlefield.

hunks.baseline: Well over a thousand of his own men were jammed at the narrow mouth and couldn’t advance. The wandering martial artists and mounted bandits he’d put at the front had numbers, but man for man they were worse than even the Jin Family’s rank-and-file.
hunks.sol: Well over a thousand of his men were jammed at the narrow entrance, unable to advance. The wandering martial artists and mounted bandits he had placed at the front had numbers on their side, but individually, they were inferior even to the Jin Family’s rank-and-file warriors.

hunks.baseline: Just as he was clicking his tongue, several dozen wandering martial artists suddenly started peeling off the front line. The middle-aged wanderer at their head bellowed until his throat tore.
hunks.sol: Just as he clicked his tongue inwardly, several dozen wandering martial artists suddenly began peeling away from the front line. The middle-aged wanderer leading them bellowed at the top of his lungs.

hunks.baseline: “This is a dog’s death! Brothers of the Blood Rain Group, fall back!”
hunks.sol: “We’ll die like dogs at this rate! Brothers of the Blood Rain Group, fall back!”

hunks.baseline: A light breeze. The wandering martial artist felt nothing else.
hunks.sol: A light breeze brushed past him. The wandering martial artist felt nothing else.

hunks.baseline: He did not know that Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek had already brushed past him. He did not know that the wandering martial artists under him had frozen in terror.
hunks.sol: He never realized that Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek had already passed him, or that his men had frozen in terror.

hunks.baseline: “Blood Rain Group, was it?”
hunks.sol: “The Blood Rain Group, was it?”

hunks.baseline: Lee Cheonbaek pointed his sword at the frozen wanderers. Not a drop of blood stained the blade.
hunks.sol: Lee Cheonbaek pointed his sword at the petrified wanderers. Not a single drop of blood stained its blade.

hunks.baseline: “Go back.”
hunks.sol: “Get back in there.”

hunks.baseline: A Peak master’s killing intent shot into them like a blade. The wandering martial artists charged toward the front even faster than they had come.
hunks.sol: The killing intent of a Peak master lashed out like a blade. The wandering martial artists charged toward the front even faster than they had retreated.

hunks.baseline: They had decided that fighting at the front beat throwing themselves at the Peak master in front of them.
hunks.sol: They had decided that fighting on the front line was better than throwing themselves at the Peak master before them.

hunks.baseline: Lee Cheonbaek went after them. His burning gaze was aimed somewhere ahead, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s command had to be.
hunks.sol: Lee Cheonbaek followed after them. His blazing gaze was fixed somewhere ahead, where the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s leaders had to be.

hunks.baseline: With Lee Cheonbaek stepping forward, the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s core forces followed.
hunks.sol: As Lee Cheonbaek stepped forward, the Mount Heng Sword Sect’s core forces followed.

hunks.baseline: Three Peak masters and dozens of First Rate masters crashed toward the front.
hunks.sol: Three Peak masters and dozens of First Rate masters surged toward the front.
